name: S&P Global
description: S&P Global sells the information and benchmarks that financial markets run on. Ratings assigns credit ratings and is paid by the companies and governments that issue debt, so its revenue follows how much debt is sold. Indices (S&P Dow Jones Indices) licenses index names such as the S&P 500 and earns fees on assets invested in products tracking them plus data subscriptions. Market Intelligence sells desktop data and analytics subscriptions to banks and asset managers. Energy (formerly Commodity Insights, including Platts price benchmarks) sells price data to commodity traders. Mobility (Carfax and automotive data) was distributed to shareholders on July 1, 2026 as a separate company, so the business now reports four segments.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge, not re-checked. SEC SIC code is 7320 (Consumer Credit Reporting, Collection Agencies).

hq.note: From general knowledge; cover page not re-read in this pass. Incorporated in New York in December 1925 (10-K).

employees.note: Permanent employees worldwide, including Mobility, which was spun off on July 1, 2026 (so the go-forward figure is lower)

businessLines.name: Market Intelligence
businessLines.how: Annual and multi-year subscriptions for data, research, analytics and workflow software (Capital IQ), paid by financial firms per user or per data feed.

businessLines.name: Ratings
businessLines.how: Issuers pay a fee based on the size of each bond or loan rated, so issuance volume drives it, plus annual surveillance fees on rated debt and licensing of ratings content.

revenue.note: External revenue; $4,724M including $175M intersegment royalty charged to Market Intelligence

businessLines.revenueNote: External revenue; $4,724M including $175M intersegment royalty charged to Market Intelligence

businessLines.name: Energy (formerly Commodity Insights)
businessLines.how: Subscriptions to commodity price assessments (Platts), news, analytics and data, plus fees for licensing price benchmarks used in contracts.

businessLines.name: Mobility (spun off July 1, 2026 as Mobility Global, NYSE: MBGL)
businessLines.how: Subscriptions and per-report fees for vehicle history, automotive market data and analytics sold to manufacturers, dealers and lenders.

businessLines.name: Indices (S&P Dow Jones Indices)
businessLines.how: A basis-point fee on assets in funds and ETFs that track its indices, plus licence fees on exchange-traded derivatives and subscriptions to index data.
